notes.text: Egor Chinakhov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 15 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 99:40 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Atley Calvert was added to the roster on Nov 27 and has played beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 10th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Brandon Carlo is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. Colton Parayko has taken his spot beside Cam Fowler. That pair has had 39% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 32:33 together, down from 54% with Carlo.
Jimmy Snuggerud is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Jake Neighbours has taken his spot beside Robert Thomas and Dylan Holloway.

story.head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Blues won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Pittsburgh on Nov 19. The Penguins (8-15-2) beat Buffalo 6-3 on Friday, and the Blues (14-9-3) beat Dallas 5-3 the same night. Going in, the Pens are last in the Metropolitan (31st in the NHL) and the Blues sixth in the Central (tied for 14th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.360) says: their chances are worth about .531, mostly because they’re 4-8 in one-goal games. The Blues’ record (.596) is about what their chances are worth.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). On the other side, the Blues get the league’s best looks (1st), keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and rarely ice the puck (2nd). The Penguins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Blues, and the Penguins are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blues.

Evgeni Malkin (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 21 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Tommy Novak (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 25 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Pittsburgh. Dylan Holloway (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 26 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with seven points in his last five games.
Artūrs Šilovs (5-9-1 / .873 SV% in 15 GS) is in line to start for Pittsburgh. Joel Hofer (11-6-2 / .919 SV% in 19 GS) has been a rock in net for St. Louis and will likely start.
At home, Jim Montgomery likes to send Toropchenko, Suter and Dvorský out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Dewar, Lizotte and Calvert.
